note: Derived from analysis/classify.py, the rule set that recovered 80 of the 85 labelled pull requests in the case study corpus. Scored by tools/corpus-check.mjs. 'strong' matches anywhere in title or body; 'weak' matches count only in the title at medium confidence, because these words appear in ordinary prose in any repository that uses the tools they name.
limits: This reads pull request prose, so it measures how often a failure was written about. Two categories are known to under-report for structural reasons: runner contention is a property of the CI system rather than of any pull request (in the case study the median pull request waited eleven minutes for a runner while only two narrated it), and migration chain forks frequently occur between pushes and are repaired before review, so no pull request ever mentions them. Both need --deep or the gates in scripts/ to see properly.

categories.label: Rework / supersede
categories.gate: scripts/check_paths_owned.sh — overlapping ownership is what makes one lane rewrite another

categories.label: Cross-lane dependency
